hook.evidence: 'Did you know honey basically never goes bad?' — a premise phrased exactly in the generic 'Did you know…' form.

structure.evidence: Setup (never goes bad) -> evidence (tombs) -> three reasons -> 'That's why your honey jar can sit in the cupboard for years.' Payoff present, but the last line 'next time you see crystallised honey… just warm it up' is an off-topic filler beat.

clarity.evidence: Plain cause-and-effect a listener can retell ('very little water in it, so bacteria can't grow'); between 3 and 5 because the crystallisation tip introduces a new unexplained idea at the end.

pace.evidence: 95 spoken words / 30 s = 3.17 wps, inside 2.0-3.2 but above 2.8; long lines like 'Archaeologists have reported finding pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that were still edible.' (15 words); no visual cues marked.

accuracy.evidence: Main claims plausible and the tomb claim hedged ('have reported'), but no source given for any claim (water content, peroxide, acidity).

voice.evidence: Consistent, friendly explainer tone ('basically', 'really hard for microbes to survive') with little personality; could be many channels.

notes: Pace counts spoken words only (brackets excluded, punctuation-only tokens excluded) over 30 s target.
